summary: Second-order linear equation. 1 method applies: Characteristic equation.

methods.name: Characteristic equation
methods.reason: The equation is linear and homogeneous with constant coefficients.

steps.title: Write the characteristic equation
steps.text: For constant coefficients, try \(y = e^{rx}\). Substituting and dividing by \(e^{rx}\) leaves a quadratic in \(r\).

steps.title: Solve for the roots
steps.text: The discriminant is negative, so the roots are complex, \(r = \alpha \pm \beta i\). They give \(e^{\alpha x}\cos \beta x\) and \(e^{\alpha x}\sin \beta x\).

steps.title: Write the general solution
steps.text: Combine the two independent solutions with arbitrary constants.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked symbolically by substituting back into the equation.

methods.verify_note: Checked symbolically by substituting back into the equation.

methods.name: Undetermined coefficients
methods.reason: The right-hand side is 0, so there is no particular solution to guess.

methods.name: Variation of parameters
methods.reason: The right-hand side is 0, so no particular solution is needed.

methods.name: Cauchy–Euler (y = x^r)
methods.reason: The equation does not have the form \(ax^2 y'' + bx y' + c y = 0\).

methods.name: Laplace transform
methods.reason: It needs initial conditions at \(x = 0\); add them to see this method.
